messages:
maya: Heads-up — compliance asked whether exports can include the routing policy state at the exact time of the change (not just the diff). Need product opinion because it affects export size and PII surface.
alex: is this for the UI preview or the NDJSON export?
maya: both. They want a tiny in-console snapshot for quick triage + full snapshot option in exports for e-discovery.
jon: heavy: storing full routing snapshots for every change will bloat the audit ledger. Do we even have the schema to serialize 'resolved routing' (tenant, route, conditions, quota-bindings)?
priya: we can materialize a compact snapshot: only store rule IDs + evaluated key-values used to decide routing. That keeps size down and still shows who/why route picked.
alex: +1 for compact. Also we should keep an option: "include-resolved-routing=true" on export API so downstream consumers opt-in. Default false.
maya: product wants the console UX to show the resolved routing without requiring export. Could be a small expandable panel labeled "Routing snapshot (evaluated)". Privacy flagged entries should redact by default.
jon: telemetry question — if we materialize resolved routing at write time, we can emit a routing-evaluated metric for every change. That helps QA / regressions, but it's extra cardinality. Ops-bot: you will be charged for the extra metrics. :grimacing:
priya: can we instead compute resolved routing on-demand when someone previews an event in the console? That avoids storage but adds latency to preview and needs the same evaluation code available for historical snapshots (model drift / rule evolution problem).
alex: on-demand eval means we must preserve the exact rule version used. Otherwise the resolved result could differ later. So we either snapshot small bits now or store rule-version pointers to reproduce later. Both add complexity.
maya: two proposals: (A) Snapshot compact evaluated data at change time (rule IDs, key-values, route id, policy version) and store with audit event. (B) Store rule-version pointer + raw inputs and evaluate on-demand. Which is less risky for compliance?
priya: A is simpler for compliance audits (immutable evidence). B is smaller but requires replay infra and guarantees about rule-version immutability.
jon: also note export-volume impact. If we add compact snapshots to every audit event, estimates: +400 bytes/event on average -> +40GB/month for high-activity tenants. Need quota implications and download cost warnings.
maya: product is fine if we gate full snapshots behind the export flag and keep console preview to the compact snapshot only. That reduces export size unless customer explicitly opts in.
alex: implementational detail — API shape suggestion: /v1/audits?include_resolved_routing=compact|full. compact = our default snapshot, full = expanded rule text + matched clause bodies.
priya: also need a PII mode: include_resolved_routing=compact but pii=redact|include. default redact. Compliance teams will request include sometimes, with data-access guardrails.
jon: rollout plan: behind a feature flag per-tenant, and soft quota that warns admins in console when export size > X. We'll also add a per-tenant meter for additional storage.
maya: typo — we'll need a console affordance: when a user tries to download full snapshots, show a modal: "This export may include sensitive routing policy bodies. Confirm and record justification." Store justification as part of export audit.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: new feature flag created: ff/audit-routing-snapshots. Owner: @jon.
alex: open question — how to represent the compact snapshot schema in the export NDJSON? proposal: {"route_id":"r-123","policy_version":"v42","matched_keys":{"path":"/v1","tenant_tier":"enterprise"},"decision":"allow"} as a single field on the audit event.
jon: fine. add a schema version field so we can evolve later: routing_snapshot_v = 1.
maya: ok next steps: priya + jon draft compact schema and size estimates; alex to update API params and console modal copy; i'll sync with legal about retention/PII guardrails.
priya: i'll start a short prototype that appends ~250-600B per event depending on rule complexity and share numbers.
jon: thanks. tagging @ops-bot so infra knows potential cardinality and metric impact.
maya: thanks all — we'll discuss in infra sync tomorrow if there are heavy objections.
